scenes.heading: Multiplying and dividing integers
scenes.say: Is negative two to the power of five positive or negative? What about negative two to the power of four? In this video you'll learn one simple idea that answers both: count the negatives.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Each U-turn on a path flips the way you face
scenes.science: Each negative factor flips the sign; pairs of negatives cancel
scenes.breaks: a U-turn doesn't change distance, but multiplying by −3 also makes the size three times bigger.
scenes.say: Imagine walking along a path. Every negative number is a U-turn. One U-turn and you face backwards. Two U-turns and you face forwards again. So an even number of negatives gives a positive answer, and an odd number gives a negative answer. You still multiply the sizes as normal.

scenes.heading: The rules
points: × and ÷ are equal: go left to right
scenes.say: Here are the rules. Work out the size first, then the sign. An even number of negatives gives a positive. An odd number gives a negative. And multiply and divide have equal rank, so go from left to right.

scenes.heading: Four jumps of −3
scenes.say: Why is four times negative three negative? Start at zero and make four jumps of negative three to the left: negative three, negative six, negative nine, negative twelve. So four times negative three is negative twelve. Dividing undoes it: negative twelve split into four equal jumps gives negative three each.
scenes.caption: Start at 0 and make four jumps of −3: −3, −6, −9, −12. So 4 × (−3) = −12, and −12 ÷ 4 = −3.

scenes.heading: A long product
scenes.question: Work out (−4) × 6 × (−5) × (−1).
scenes.say: Negative four times six times negative five times negative one. Size first: four times six times five times one is one hundred and twenty. Now count the negatives: there are three. Three is odd, so the answer is negative one hundred and twenty.
scenes.caption: (−4) × 6 × (−5) × (−1). Size: 4 × 6 × 5 × 1 = 120. Three negatives is odd, so the answer is −120.

scenes.heading: Brackets matter with powers
scenes.say: Watch the brackets. In brackets negative three to the power of four, the whole negative three is multiplied four times. Four negatives is even, so it's eighty-one. But negative three to the power of four without brackets means only the three is powered, then the minus goes on the front: negative eighty-one.
scenes.caption: (−3)⁴: the whole −3 is multiplied four times. Four negatives is even, so it's 81. But −3⁴ means only the 3 is powered, then the minus goes on: −81.

scenes.heading: Left to right
scenes.question: Work out −96 ÷ 8 × (−3).
scenes.say: Negative ninety-six divided by eight, times negative three. Divide and multiply are equal, so go left to right. Negative ninety-six divided by eight is negative twelve. Negative twelve times negative three is thirty-six.
scenes.caption: −96 ÷ 8 × (−3). Go left to right. −96 ÷ 8 = −12. −12 × (−3) = 36.

scenes.heading: Roots
points: A negative has no ordinary square root
scenes.say: Square roots: both seven and negative seven square to forty-nine, and the root symbol means the positive one, seven. A negative number has no ordinary square root. But cube roots of negatives are fine: the cube root of negative twenty-seven is negative three.
scenes.caption: Both 7 and −7 square to 49, and √49 means the positive one, 7. A negative number has no ordinary square root. But ∛(−27) = −3.

points: Check a division by multiplying back
scenes.say: Quick recap. Size first, then sign. Count the negatives: even is positive, odd is negative. Brackets matter with powers. And check every division by multiplying back. Now try the practice questions!
